# `device` reference

Every method of the `device` global, with its arguments, return value,
errors, where it works, and an example. The
[Device API guide](https://ganymede-server.com/docs/ganymede-ui/device)
explains where `device` exists and how to call it from a server kernel
or a browser.

`device` is `undefined` on kernels the app doesn't host, so a cell
checks for it first (`device?.clipboard.readText()`, or
`if (device) …`). The examples skip that check, and the
[`SoundPlayer`](#soundplayer) examples use a `player` from
[`device.sound.player`](#device-sound-player-data-options), and the
[`Peripheral`](#peripheral) examples a `peripheral` from
[`device.bluetooth.connect`](#device-bluetooth-connect-id-options).

For editor types, add this line once to a cell or a project file:

```ts
/// <reference types="@tlockney/ganymede-device/globals" />
```

Every method takes a last `options` argument with a `signal`
([`CallOptions`](#calloptions)), and fails with a
[`DeviceError`](#errors). **Availability** says where each method
works: in the app (a kernel the Mac, iPad or iPhone app runs itself),
the system permission it needs there, from a [remote
kernel](https://ganymede-server.com/docs/ganymede-ui/device#from-a-server-kernel)
in the app, and from a kernel driven from a
[browser](https://ganymede-server.com/docs/ganymede-ui/device#in-a-browser).
"planned" means it doesn't yet but will; "no" means the platform has no
such API.

## `device`

The `device` global: native features of the Mac, iPad and iPhone apps.
Undefined on kernels the app doesn't host, so check for it first.

### `device.info(options?)`

```ts
info(options?: CallOptions): Promise<DeviceInfo>;
```

Reads what the host is and the device's current state.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<DeviceInfo>`: The host's answer to `hello` as it was when the kernel started, with the current screen, battery, appearance and locale where the host reads them.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | yes |

A browser has no model or battery.

```ts
const info = await device.info();
console.log(info.platform, info.osVersion, info.battery?.level);
```

### `device.has(method)`

```ts
has(method: string): boolean;
```

Whether the host answers a method. Synchronous: it reads what the host
said when the kernel started, so it can't be cancelled.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `method` | `string` | yes | A method's name as `SUPPORT` lists it, such as `"clipboard.readText"` or `"openURL"`. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `true` when the host answers it; calling a method it doesn't fails `unavailable`.

```ts
if (device.has("haptics.impact")) await device.haptics.impact();
else console.log("no haptics on", (await device.info()).platform);
```

### `device.on(event, handler, options?)`

```ts
on<E extends HostEvent>(event: E, handler: (value: HostEvents[E]) => void, options?: OnOptions): () => void;
```

Calls `handler` each time the device changes in the way `event`
names, until it is removed: by calling the function `on` answers, by
aborting `options.signal`, or by a kernel restart. Unlike other calls,
an interrupt leaves it running, since it outlives the cell that added
it. A handler that runs after its cell finished writes its output
where the kernel sends output with no running cell, so keep handlers
to updating state or a display by id. No permission; in the app only.
When the host can't send events, the handler is removed and one line
on stderr says why; `has("on")` tells beforehand.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `event` | `E` | yes | What to watch: `appearance`, `foreground`, `background`, `battery` or `locale`. |
| `handler` | `(value: HostEvents[E]) => void` | yes | Called with the event's value (`HostEvents`). An error it throws goes to stderr and doesn't remove it. |
| `options` | `OnOptions` | no | The `signal` that removes the handler. |

**Returns** `() => void`: A function that removes the handler.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` when `event` isn't one of the five or `handler` isn't a function.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | no | no |

Appearance, foreground, background, battery and locale changes; an interrupt doesn't remove a handler.

```ts
const off = device.on("appearance", (mode) => console.log("now", mode));
// Later, in any cell:
off();
```

### `device.openURL(url, options?)`

```ts
openURL(url: string | URL, options?: OpenURLOptions): Promise<void>;
```

Opens a link: in the browser, or the mail app for `mailto`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | `string \| URL` | yes | An `http`, `https` or `mailto` URL. |
| `options` | `OpenURLOptions` | no | `inApp` shows a web page in the app on iPhone and iPad, and the call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`; the URL may already have opened. |

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` for any other scheme.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | after a click |

http, https and mailto only. `inApp` works on iPhone and iPad, not the Mac; a browser opens a tab after a click, and ignores `inApp`.

```ts
await device.openURL("https://ganymede-server.com/docs/", { inApp: true });
```

### `device.share(options)`

```ts
share(options: ShareOptions): Promise<boolean>;
```

Shows the system share sheet (`NSSharingServicePicker` on the Mac).
The sheet is its own consent, so no permission.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `ShareOptions` | yes | `text`, `url` and `files` to share (at least one; files together at most 16 MiB), and the call's `signal`, which closes the sheet and rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<boolean>`: `true` when the person picked where to send them (on iPhone and iPad once the share completes; on the Mac as soon as they pick a service), `false` when they dismissed it.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` when there is nothing to share, a file has no plain name, or the files are over 16 MiB.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | after a click |

The share sheet; `NSSharingServicePicker` on the Mac. A browser uses the Web Share API, after a click, and shares files only where it can.

```ts
const csv = "city,temp\nOslo,4\nLima,19\n";
await device.share({
  text: "Today's temperatures",
  files: [{ name: "temps.csv", data: new TextEncoder().encode(csv) }],
});
```

### `device.preview(files, options?)`

```ts
preview(files: NamedBytes[], options?: CallOptions): Promise<void>;
```

Shows files in Quick Look. Quick Look picks the viewer from each
name's extension, so name a PNG `*.png`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `files` | `NamedBytes[]` | yes | The files, together at most 16 MiB. |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`, which closes Quick Look and rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** once the person closes it.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` when `files` is empty, a file has no plain name, or the files are over 16 MiB.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | no |

Quick Look, which picks the viewer from each file name's extension. A browser has no Quick Look.

```ts
const png = await device.clipboard.readImage();
if (png) await device.preview([{ name: "clipboard.png", data: png }]);
```

### Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `clipboard` | `Clipboard` | The system clipboard: see `Clipboard`. |
| `haptics` | `Haptics` | Taptic feedback, on iPhone: see `Haptics`. |
| `ui` | `UI` | Dialogs over the notebook: see `UI`. |
| `files` | `Files` | The system's file pickers: see `Files`. |
| `photos` | `Photos` | The system photo picker: see `Photos`. |
| `sound` | `Sound` | Sound playback: see `Sound`. |
| `notifications` | `Notifications` | Local notifications after a delay: see `Notifications`. |
| `location` | `DeviceLocation` | Where the device is, and geocoding: see `DeviceLocation`. |
| `motion` | `DeviceMotion` | The motion sensors, on iPad and iPhone: see `DeviceMotion`. |
| `contacts` | `Contacts` | The person's contacts: see `Contacts`. |
| `camera` | `Camera` | The system camera: see `Camera`. |
| `reminders` | `Reminders` | The person's reminders: see `Reminders`. |
| `bluetooth` | `Bluetooth` | Bluetooth LE peripherals: see `Bluetooth`. |
| `folders` | `Folders` | Folders the person picked for this notebook: see `Folders`. |
| `secrets` | `Secrets` | Strings this notebook saved in the keychain: see `Secrets`. |

## `device.clipboard`

The system clipboard. iPadOS may show its paste prompt on a read.

### `device.clipboard.readText(options?)`

```ts
readText(options?: CallOptions): Promise<string | null>;
```

Reads the clipboard's text.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<string | null>`: The text, or `null` when the clipboard holds none.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | after a click |

iPadOS shows its paste prompt; a browser needs a click for the Clipboard API.

```ts
const text = await device.clipboard.readText();
if (text !== null) console.log(text.split(/\s+/).length, "words");
```

### `device.clipboard.writeText(text, options?)`

```ts
writeText(text: string, options?: CallOptions): Promise<void>;
```

Replaces the clipboard's contents with `text`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `string` | yes | The text to copy. |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`; the write may already have happened. |

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | after a click |

A browser needs a click for the Clipboard API.

```ts
await device.clipboard.writeText(JSON.stringify({ rows: 3 }, null, 2));
```

### `device.clipboard.readImage(options?)`

```ts
readImage(options?: CallOptions): Promise<Uint8Array | null>;
```

Reads the clipboard's image as PNG bytes, whatever format was copied.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<Uint8Array | null>`: PNG bytes, or `null` when the clipboard holds no image.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | after a click |

PNG. iPadOS shows its paste prompt; a browser needs a click for the Clipboard API.

```ts
const png = await device.clipboard.readImage();
if (png) console.log(`${png.byteLength} bytes`);
```

### `device.clipboard.writeImage(image, options?)`

```ts
writeImage(image: Bytes, options?: CallOptions): Promise<void>;
```

Replaces the clipboard's contents with an image.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `image` | `Bytes` | yes | PNG, JPEG, GIF, HEIC or TIFF bytes, at most 16 MiB. |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`; the write may already have happened. |

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` when the bytes aren't an image the device reads.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | after a click |

A browser needs a click for the Clipboard API, and takes PNG only.

```ts
const [photo] = await device.photos.pick();
if (photo) await device.clipboard.writeImage(photo);
```

Taptic feedback. iPhone only: iPads and Macs have no Taptic Engine, so
there `device.has("haptics.impact")` is false and calls fail
`unavailable`.

| `style` | `ImpactStyle` | no | How strong a tap: `"light"`, `"medium"` (the default), `"heavy"`, `"soft"` or `"rigid"`. |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`; the tap may already have played. |

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| iPhone | none | yes | no |

iPhone only: iPads and Macs have no Taptic Engine. A browser has no haptics API Safari supports.

```ts
if (device.has("haptics.impact")) await device.haptics.impact("heavy");
```

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| iPhone | none | yes | no |

iPhone only: iPads and Macs have no Taptic Engine.

iPhone only: iPads and Macs have no Taptic Engine.

```ts
for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
```

## `device.ui`

Dialogs the app shows over the notebook: sheets on the Mac, alerts on
iPhone and iPad. One shows at a time; a second call waits for the first
to close. Dismissing one is not an error: it returns `null` or `false`.
An interrupt or an aborted `signal` closes it and rejects `cancelled`
(`timeout` for `AbortSignal.timeout()`).

### `device.ui.alert(message, options?)`

```ts
alert(message: string, options?: AlertOptions): Promise<void>;
```

Shows a message with an OK button.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | `string` | yes | The message. |
| `options` | `AlertOptions` | no | `title` is a heading above it; `signal` cancels: it closes the alert and rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** once the person closes it.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | planned |

A sheet on the Mac, an alert on iPhone and iPad; a browser will show it in the cell's output.

```ts
await device.ui.alert("The import finished: 1,204 rows.", { title: "Done" });
```

### `device.ui.confirm(message, options?)`

```ts
confirm(message: string, options?: ConfirmOptions): Promise<boolean>;
```

Asks a yes-or-no question.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | `string` | yes | The question. |
| `options` | `ConfirmOptions` | no | `title`, `okLabel` for the confirming button, `destructive` to show it red, and the call's `signal`. |

**Returns** `Promise<boolean>`: `true` when the person confirms, `false` when they cancel or dismiss it.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | planned |

```ts
if (await device.ui.confirm("Delete the scratch files?", { destructive: true, okLabel: "Delete" })) {
  console.log("deleting");
}
```

### `device.ui.prompt(message, options?)`

```ts
prompt(message: string, options?: PromptOptions): Promise<string | null>;
```

Asks for a line of text.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | `string` | yes | The question. |
| `options` | `PromptOptions` | no | `title`, `placeholder`, `defaultValue`, `secure` to hide what is typed, and the call's `signal`. |

**Returns** `Promise<string | null>`: The text entered, or `null` when the person cancels.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | planned |

```ts
const name = await device.ui.prompt("Name the run", { defaultValue: "baseline" });
if (name !== null) console.log(`saving ${name}`);
```

### `device.ui.actionSheet(title, options, sheetOptions?)`

```ts
actionSheet(title: string, options: string[], sheetOptions?: ActionSheetOptions): Promise<number | null>;
```

Asks the person to choose one of several options.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | yes | The sheet's heading. |
| `options` | `string[]` | yes | The choices' labels, at least one. |
| `sheetOptions` | `ActionSheetOptions` | no | `message` under the title, `cancel` for the cancel button's label, `destructive` for the index of an option to show red, and the call's `signal`. |

**Returns** `Promise<number | null>`: The index of the option chosen, or `null` when the person cancels.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` when `options` is empty.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | planned |

```ts
const formats = ["CSV", "JSON", "Parquet"];
const i = await device.ui.actionSheet("Export as", formats);
if (i !== null) console.log(`exporting ${formats[i]}`);
```

Asks for a date, a time, or both.

| `options` | `PickDateOptions` | no | `mode` (`"date"`, `"time"` or `"datetime"`, the default), `title`, `value` to start at, `min` and `max`, and the call's `signal`. |

**Returns** `Promise<Date | null>`: The date chosen, or `null` when the person cancels.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` when `value`, `min` or `max` isn't a valid `Date`.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | planned |

```ts
const start = await device.ui.pickDate({ mode: "date", title: "Report from", max: new Date() });
if (start) console.log(start.toISOString().slice(0, 10));
```

## `device.files`

Files in and out through the system's own pickers, which are the
person's consent, so no permission. A picked file is copied in by value:
the notebook keeps no access to where it came from.

### `device.files.pick(options?)`

```ts
pick(options?: PickFilesOptions): Promise<File[]>;
```

Shows the open panel on the Mac, or the document picker on iPad and
iPhone, and reads the files the person picks. Together they are at
most 16 MiB.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `PickFilesOptions` | no | `types` limits what can be picked, `multiple` allows more than one, and `signal` cancels: it closes the picker and rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<File[]>`: The picked files, with their names and MIME types, or `[]` when the person cancels.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` when `types` or `multiple` has the wrong type, or the files together are over 16 MiB.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | after a click |

The open panel on the Mac, the document picker on iPad and iPhone. Files are copied in; no access to where they came from is kept. A browser can't filter by a type identifier such as `public.json`, so with one it allows any file.

```ts
const [file] = await device.files.pick({ types: [".csv", "text/csv"] });
if (file) {
  const rows = (await file.text()).trim().split("\n");
  console.log(file.name, rows.length, "rows");
}
```

### `device.files.export(data, options)`

```ts
export(data: Bytes, options: ExportFileOptions): Promise<boolean>;
```

Asks where to save `data`, and saves it there: the save panel on the
Mac, the document picker on iPad and iPhone.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | `Bytes` | yes | The file's contents, at most 16 MiB. |
| `options` | `ExportFileOptions` | yes | `name` is the file name the panel suggests; `signal` cancels: it closes the panel and rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<boolean>`: `true` when saved, `false` when the person cancels.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` when `name` isn't a plain file name, or `data` is over 16 MiB.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | after a click |

The save panel on the Mac, the document picker on iPad and iPhone. A browser downloads it after a click, and answers `true` then, since it can't tell whether it was saved.

```ts
const csv = "city,temp\nOslo,4\nLima,19\n";
const saved = await device.files.export(new TextEncoder().encode(csv), { name: "temps.csv" });
console.log(saved ? "saved" : "cancelled");
```

## `device.photos`

The photo library: the system photo picker to read photos, which needs
no permission, and `save` to add one, which needs add-only access. The
permission methods are about that add-only access: the first `save`
asks (the app's prompt for this notebook, then the system's), and a
refusal rejects `denied`. Granted, `authorizationStatus()` reads
`writeOnly`: the app may add photos, never read the library.

The permission methods (`authorizationStatus`, `isAuthorized`, `requestAuthorization`) are about `save`'s add-only access, and work where `save` does: in the app, not from a remote kernel or a browser.

### `device.photos.authorizationStatus(options?)`

```ts
authorizationStatus(options?: CallOptions): Promise<AuthorizationStatus>;
```

Reads the permission's status, without asking.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<AuthorizationStatus>`: `"notDetermined"` until the person is asked, then a grant (`"authorized"`, or a partial one) or `"denied"` or `"restricted"`.

```ts
console.log(await device.photos.authorizationStatus());
```

### `device.photos.isAuthorized(options?)`

```ts
isAuthorized(options?: CallOptions): Promise<boolean>;
```

Whether the permission is granted, without asking.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<boolean>`: `true` when the status is a grant, partial ones included.

```ts
if (!(await device.photos.isAuthorized())) console.log("not allowed yet");
```

### `device.photos.requestAuthorization(options?)`

```ts
requestAuthorization(options?: CallOptions): Promise<AuthorizationStatus>;
```

Asks the person when they haven't been asked (the app's prompt for
this notebook, then the system's where there is one), and
resolves with the status after it; otherwise resolves with the status
as it is. The namespace's methods ask on their own, so calling this
first is optional. Cancel rejects `cancelled`; a system prompt already
up stays, and its answer still counts for later calls.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. |

**Returns** `Promise<AuthorizationStatus>`: The status after the prompt, or as it was when the person had already been asked.

```ts
const status = await device.photos.requestAuthorization();
if (status === "denied") console.log("allow it in Settings to go on");
```

### `device.photos.pick(options?)`

```ts
pick(options?: PickPhotosOptions): Promise<File[]>;
```

Shows the system photo picker and reads the photos the person picks.
The picker shows the library without the app being let in, so no
permission. Together the photos are at most 16 MiB.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `PickPhotosOptions` | no | `limit` is how many may be picked (1 by default, 0 for no limit); `signal` cancels: it closes the picker and rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<File[]>`: The picked photos as image `File`s in their stored format (often HEIC or JPEG), or `[]` when the person cancels.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` when `limit` isn't a whole number of 0 or more, or the photos together are over 16 MiB.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | after a click |

The system photo picker, which needs no photo library permission. A browser shows a file picker for images, and keeps the first `limit` picked.

```ts
const photos = await device.photos.pick({ limit: 3 });
for (const photo of photos) console.log(photo.name, photo.type, photo.size);
```

### `device.photos.save(image, options?)`

```ts
save(image: Bytes, options?: CallOptions): Promise<void>;
```

Adds an image to the photo library, as a new photo.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `image` | `Bytes` | yes | PNG, JPEG, GIF, HEIC or TIFF bytes, or a `Blob` of them, at most 16 MiB. |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`; the photo may already have been added. |

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `denied` when the notebook or the system may not add photos; `failed` when the bytes aren't PNG, JPEG, GIF, HEIC or TIFF, or the library refuses them.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | photos | no | no |

Add-only access: the app may add photos, never read the library.

```ts
const canvas = new OffscreenCanvas(256, 256);
const g = canvas.getContext("2d")!;
g.fillStyle = "teal";
g.fillRect(0, 0, 256, 256);
await device.photos.save(await canvas.convertToBlob({ type: "image/png" }));
```

## `device.sound`

Sound from bytes in any format the device reads (WAV, AIFF, MP3,
AAC/M4A, CAF, FLAC), at most 16 MiB. No permission. On iPhone the
ring/silent switch can silence it.

### `device.sound.play(data, options?)`

```ts
play(data: Bytes, options?: PlaySoundOptions): Promise<void>;
```

Starts playing a sound, which plays to its end on its own.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | `Bytes` | yes | The sound's bytes, at most 16 MiB. |
| `options` | `PlaySoundOptions` | no | `volume` from 0 to 1 (1 by default), and the call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`; the sound may already be playing. |

**Returns** once the sound has started.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` when `data` is empty, over 16 MiB, or not a sound the device reads.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | after a click |

A browser asks for a click only until the page has had one.

```ts
const [file] = await device.files.pick({ types: ["audio/*"] });
if (file) await device.sound.play(file, { volume: 0.5 });
```

### `device.sound.player(data, options?)`

```ts
player(data: Bytes, options?: CallOptions): Promise<SoundPlayer>;
```

Loads a sound into a player, paused at the start, for a cell to play,
pause, seek and close. A kernel has at most 32 open at once.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | `Bytes` | yes | The sound's bytes, at most 16 MiB. |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. |

**Returns** `Promise<SoundPlayer>`: A `SoundPlayer`.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` when `data` is empty, over 16 MiB, or not a sound the device reads, or the kernel has 32 players open.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | no | no |

Play, pause, stop, seek and volume; close it, or hold it with `await using`. Remote kernels and browsers: a handle wouldn't survive a disconnect.

```ts
const [file] = await device.files.pick({ types: ["audio/*"] });
if (file) {
  await using player = await device.sound.player(file);
  await player.play();
  // Leaving the block closes the player, which stops it: wait for the end.
  await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, player.duration * 1000));
}
```

## `device.notifications`

Local notifications after a delay: the app posts them even when the
notebook or the app is closed. Delay only, no calendar times or
repeats. Each notification belongs to the notebook that scheduled it:
`pending()`, `cancel()` and `cancelAll()` see only that notebook's.

Needs the notifications permission, for `schedule()`: the first call
asks (the app's prompt for this notebook, then the system's) and a
refusal rejects `denied`. `authorizationStatus()`, `isAuthorized()` and
`requestAuthorization()` read and ask for it.

The permission methods (`authorizationStatus`, `isAuthorized`, `requestAuthorization`) work where the rest of the namespace does: in the app, not from a remote kernel or a browser.

### `device.notifications.authorizationStatus(options?)`

```ts
authorizationStatus(options?: CallOptions): Promise<AuthorizationStatus>;
```

Reads the permission's status, without asking.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<AuthorizationStatus>`: `"notDetermined"` until the person is asked, then a grant (`"authorized"`, or a partial one) or `"denied"` or `"restricted"`.

```ts
console.log(await device.notifications.authorizationStatus());
```

### `device.notifications.isAuthorized(options?)`

```ts
isAuthorized(options?: CallOptions): Promise<boolean>;
```

Whether the permission is granted, without asking.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<boolean>`: `true` when the status is a grant, partial ones included.

```ts
if (!(await device.notifications.isAuthorized())) console.log("not allowed yet");
```

### `device.notifications.requestAuthorization(options?)`

```ts
requestAuthorization(options?: CallOptions): Promise<AuthorizationStatus>;
```

Asks the person when they haven't been asked (the app's prompt for
this notebook, then the system's where there is one), and
resolves with the status after it; otherwise resolves with the status
as it is. The namespace's methods ask on their own, so calling this
first is optional. Cancel rejects `cancelled`; a system prompt already
up stays, and its answer still counts for later calls.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. |

**Returns** `Promise<AuthorizationStatus>`: The status after the prompt, or as it was when the person had already been asked.

```ts

if (status === "denied") console.log("allow it in Settings to go on");
```

### `device.notifications.schedule(body, options)`

```ts
schedule(body: string, options: ScheduleNotificationOptions): Promise<string>;
```

Schedules a notification to show after a delay, even if the notebook
or the app has closed by then. iOS and iPadOS keep at most 64 per
app, dropping the soonest beyond that.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `body` | `string` | yes | The text it shows. |
| `options` | `ScheduleNotificationOptions` | yes | `delay` in seconds (more than 0), an optional `title`, and the call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`; it may already be scheduled. |

**Returns** `Promise<string>`: Its id, for `cancel()`.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `denied` when the notifications permission is refused; `failed` when `body` is empty, `delay` isn't a finite number above 0, or `title` isn't a string.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | notifications | no | no |

After `delay` seconds, even when the notebook is closed. iOS and iPadOS keep at most 64 per app.

```ts
const id = await device.notifications.schedule("The training run should be done.", {
  title: "Check the notebook",
  delay: 30 * 60,
});
```

### `device.notifications.pending(options?)`

```ts
pending(options?: CallOptions): Promise<PendingNotification[]>;
```

Lists this notebook's notifications that haven't been delivered yet.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<PendingNotification[]>`: This notebook's pending notifications; other notebooks' aren't listed.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | no | no |

Only the calling notebook's.

```ts
for (const n of await device.notifications.pending()) {
  console.log(n.id, n.body, n.date?.toLocaleTimeString());
}
```

### `device.notifications.cancel(id, options?)`

```ts
cancel(id: string, options?: CallOptions): Promise<void>;
```

Takes one of this notebook's notifications off the schedule. An id
that's gone, or another notebook's, changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | yes | What `schedule()` returned. |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. |

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` when `id` is empty.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | no | no |

Only the calling notebook's.

```ts
const id = await device.notifications.schedule("Stretch", { delay: 3600 });
await device.notifications.cancel(id);
```

### `device.notifications.cancelAll(options?)`

```ts
cancelAll(options?: CallOptions): Promise<void>;
```

Takes all of this notebook's notifications off the schedule.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. |

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | no | no |

Only the calling notebook's.

```ts

```

## `device.location`

Where the device is, over Core Location, and addresses to places and
back. While in use only: the app asks for location when in use, never
always, so nothing runs once the app quits.

`current()` and `watch()` need the location permission: the first call
asks (the app's prompt for this notebook, then the system's) and a
refusal rejects `denied`. With precise location turned off for the
app, `authorizationStatus()` reads `reducedAccuracy` and fixes are
within a few kilometres. Geocoding needs no permission but does need
the network.

Over Core Location, while the app is in use only. `current` and `watch` need the location permission; geocoding needs the network but no permission. While the app is in use only. With precise location off, within a few kilometres.

```ts

```

### `device.location.watch(options?)`

```ts
watch(options?: LocationOptions): DeviceStream<LocationFix>;
```

Fixes as the device moves, for `for await`, until the loop ends or
the cell is interrupted. Keeps the newest 16 when the cell reads
slower than they come (`dropped` counts the rest).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `LocationOptions` | no | `accuracy`, as for `current()`; and the call's `signal`, which ends the stream. |

**Returns** `DeviceStream<LocationFix>`: A stream of fixes; `close()` or leaving the loop stops Core Location.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `denied` when the notebook or the system may not use location, or Location Services is off; `failed` when `accuracy` isn't one of the three, or when Core Location stops sending fixes.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | location | no | no |

Until the loop ends or the cell is interrupted; keeps the newest 16.

```ts
for await (const fix of device.location.watch({ accuracy: "block" })) {
  console.log(fix.latitude, fix.longitude);
  if (fix.speed === 0) break;
}
```

## `device.motion`

The device's motion sensors over Core Motion: attitude, rotation rate,
gravity and the person's acceleration. iPad and iPhone only; a Mac has
no motion sensors, so `has("motion.watch")` is false there.

Two ways to read, sharing one source: `watch()` for a sample every
`interval`, as when recording, and `latest()` for the newest sample, as
in a polling loop. Both need the motion permission: the app asks for
this notebook (the system has no prompt for these sensors) and a
refusal rejects `denied`.

Over Core Motion, on iPad and iPhone; a Mac has no motion sensors. `watch` and `latest` share one source. The system has no prompt for these sensors, so the permission is the app's own, per notebook. The permission methods work where the rest of the namespace does.

### `device.motion.authorizationStatus(options?)`

```ts
authorizationStatus(options?: CallOptions): Promise<AuthorizationStatus>;
```

Reads the permission's status, without asking.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<AuthorizationStatus>`: `"notDetermined"` until the person is asked, then a grant (`"authorized"`, or a partial one) or `"denied"` or `"restricted"`.

```ts
console.log(await device.motion.authorizationStatus());
```

### `device.motion.isAuthorized(options?)`

```ts
isAuthorized(options?: CallOptions): Promise<boolean>;
```

Whether the permission is granted, without asking.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<boolean>`: `true` when the status is a grant, partial ones included.

```ts
if (!(await device.motion.isAuthorized())) console.log("not allowed yet");
```

### `device.motion.requestAuthorization(options?)`

```ts
requestAuthorization(options?: CallOptions): Promise<AuthorizationStatus>;
```

Asks the person when they haven't been asked (the app's prompt for
this notebook, then the system's where there is one), and
resolves with the status after it; otherwise resolves with the status
as it is. The namespace's methods ask on their own, so calling this
first is optional. Cancel rejects `cancelled`; a system prompt already
up stays, and its answer still counts for later calls.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. |

**Returns** `Promise<AuthorizationStatus>`: The status after the prompt, or as it was when the person had already been asked.

```ts
const status = await device.motion.requestAuthorization();
if (status === "denied") console.log("allow it in Settings to go on");
```

### `device.motion.watch(options?)`

```ts
watch(options?: MotionWatchOptions): DeviceStream<MotionSample>;
```

Samples every `interval` seconds, for `for await`, until the loop
ends or the cell is interrupted. Keeps the newest 64 when the cell
reads slower than they come (`dropped` counts the rest).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `MotionWatchOptions` | no | `interval` in seconds, 0.01 to 1 (0.1 by default); and the call's `signal`, which ends the stream. |

**Returns** `DeviceStream<MotionSample>`: A stream of samples; `close()` or leaving the loop stops the sensors unless something else still reads them.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `denied` when the notebook may not use motion; `failed` when `interval` is out of range, or Core Motion stops with an error.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| iPad, iPhone | motion | no | no |

Attitude, rotation rate, gravity and acceleration every `interval` seconds (0.01 to 1); keeps the newest 64. A Mac has no motion sensors.

```ts
const samples = [];
for await (const s of device.motion.watch({ interval: 0.05 })) {
  samples.push(s.userAcceleration);
  if (samples.length === 100) break;
}
```

### `device.motion.latest(options?)`

```ts
latest(options?: CallOptions): Promise<MotionSample>;
```

The newest sample. The first call starts the sensors and waits for a
reading; they keep running while calls keep coming, and stop about
10 seconds after the last.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<MotionSample>`: The newest sample.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `denied` when the notebook may not use motion; `failed` when Core Motion stops with an error.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| iPad, iPhone | motion | no | no |

Starts the sensors and keeps them running while calls keep coming; they stop about 10 seconds after the last.

```ts
const { attitude } = await device.motion.latest();
console.log(`tilted ${((attitude.pitch * 180) / Math.PI).toFixed(0)}°`);
```

## `device.bluetooth`

A Bluetooth LE central, over Core Bluetooth: scan for peripherals,
connect, and read, write and subscribe to their characteristics. On a
Mac and an iPad or iPhone, in kernels in the app.

`scan()`, `known()` and `connect()` need the bluetooth permission: the
first call asks (the app's prompt for this notebook, then the
system's) and a refusal rejects `denied`. They reject `unavailable`
while Bluetooth is off.

A Bluetooth LE central over Core Bluetooth, on the Mac, iPad and iPhone. `scan`, `known` and `connect` need the bluetooth permission and reject `unavailable` while Bluetooth is off. A connected peripheral is a [`Peripheral`](#peripheral). The permission methods work where the rest of the namespace does.

### `device.bluetooth.authorizationStatus(options?)`

```ts
authorizationStatus(options?: CallOptions): Promise<AuthorizationStatus>;
```

Reads the permission's status, without asking.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<AuthorizationStatus>`: `"notDetermined"` until the person is asked, then a grant (`"authorized"`, or a partial one) or `"denied"` or `"restricted"`.

```ts
console.log(await device.bluetooth.authorizationStatus());
```

### `device.bluetooth.isAuthorized(options?)`

```ts
isAuthorized(options?: CallOptions): Promise<boolean>;
```

Whether the permission is granted, without asking.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<boolean>`: `true` when the status is a grant, partial ones included.

```ts
if (!(await device.bluetooth.isAuthorized())) console.log("not allowed yet");
```

### `device.bluetooth.requestAuthorization(options?)`

```ts
requestAuthorization(options?: CallOptions): Promise<AuthorizationStatus>;
```

Asks the person when they haven't been asked (the app's prompt for
this notebook, then the system's where there is one), and
resolves with the status after it; otherwise resolves with the status
as it is. The namespace's methods ask on their own, so calling this
first is optional. Cancel rejects `cancelled`; a system prompt already
up stays, and its answer still counts for later calls.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. |

**Returns** `Promise<AuthorizationStatus>`: The status after the prompt, or as it was when the person had already been asked.

```ts
const status = await device.bluetooth.requestAuthorization();
if (status === "denied") console.log("allow it in Settings to go on");
```

### `device.bluetooth.scan(options?)`

```ts
scan(options?: ScanOptions): DeviceStream<Advertisement>;
```

Advertisements from nearby peripherals, for `for await`, until the
loop ends or the cell is interrupted. Keeps the newest 128 when the
cell reads slower than they come.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `ScanOptions` | no | `services` to filter by, `allowDuplicates`, and the call's `signal`, which ends the stream. |

**Returns** `DeviceStream<Advertisement>`: A stream of advertisements; leaving the loop stops scanning.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `denied` when the notebook or the system may not use Bluetooth; `unavailable` when Bluetooth is off; `failed` when a service isn't a UUID.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | bluetooth | no | no |

Bluetooth LE only. A browser would need Web Bluetooth, which Safari doesn't have.

```ts
for await (const ad of device.bluetooth.scan({ services: ["180D"] })) {
  console.log(ad.name, ad.rssi);
  break;
}
```

### `device.bluetooth.known(ids, options?)`

```ts
known(ids: string[], options?: CallOptions): Promise<KnownPeripheral[]>;
```

Peripherals the system knows by id, such as one a past scan found, to
connect again without scanning.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ids` | `string[]` | yes | Peripheral ids from `scan()` on this device, at most 64. |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<KnownPeripheral[]>`: The ones it knows; the others are left out.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `denied` when the notebook or the system may not use Bluetooth; `unavailable` when Bluetooth is off; `failed` when an id isn't a UUID.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | bluetooth | no | no |

```ts
const [strap] = await device.bluetooth.known(["6E400001-B5A3-F393-E0A9-E50E24DCCA9E"]);
if (strap) {
  await using peripheral = await device.bluetooth.connect(strap.id);
  console.log(await peripheral.rssi());
}
```

### `device.bluetooth.connect(id, options?)`

```ts
connect(id: string, options?: ConnectOptions): Promise<Peripheral>;
```

Connects to a peripheral.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | yes | Its id, from `scan()` or `known()`. |
| `options` | `ConnectOptions` | no | `timeout` in seconds (15 by default), and the call's `signal`. Cancel stops connecting and rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<Peripheral>`: The connected peripheral, a handle to close when done.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `denied` when the notebook or the system may not use Bluetooth; `unavailable` when Bluetooth is off; `timeout` when it doesn't answer in time; `failed` when it is unknown, already connected, or the kernel has 8 connected.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | bluetooth | no | no |

Services, read, write, notify and RSSI; close it, or hold it with `await using`. At most 8 per kernel.

```ts
for await (const ad of device.bluetooth.scan({ services: ["180D"] })) {
  await using strap = await device.bluetooth.connect(ad.id);
  console.log(await strap.services());
  break;
}
```

## `device.folders`

Folders the person picked, for lasting access from this notebook: the
kernel has no file system of its own. The picker is the consent, so
there is no permission prompt; Settings lists each notebook's folders
and revokes them. Works in kernels in the app only.

Folders the person picked, kept per notebook as bookmarks, on the Mac, iPad and iPhone. No permission: the picker is the consent, and Settings revokes. A picked folder is a [`Folder`](#folder).

### `device.folders.pick(options?)`

```ts
pick(options?: PickFolderOptions): Promise<Folder | null>;
```

Shows the system folder picker and keeps what the person picks for
this notebook. Picking a folder it already has replaces that grant,
keeping its id.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `PickFolderOptions` | no | `write` to ask for writing too, and the call's `signal`, which closes the picker and rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<Folder | null>`: The folder, or `null` when the person cancelled.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `denied` when the app doesn't know which notebook this is; `failed` when access to the folder can't be kept.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | no | no |

The system folder picker, which is the consent; the folder stays the notebook's until revoked in Settings. A browser would need the File System Access API, which Safari doesn't have.

```ts
const folder = await device.folders.pick();
if (folder) console.log(folder.name, (await folder.entries()).length);
```

### `device.folders.list(options?)`

```ts
list(options?: CallOptions): Promise<Folder[]>;
```

The folders this notebook was given, in the order they were picked.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<Folder[]>`: Its folders, or `[]`.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `denied` when the app doesn't know which notebook this is.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | no | no |

A `Folder` lists, reads, writes and removes inside the folder only; reads up to 16 MiB.

```ts
const folders = await device.folders.list();
const data = folders.find((f) => f.name === "Data") ?? (await device.folders.pick());
```

## `device.secrets`

Strings this notebook saved, such as an API token, kept in the
system keychain on this device and never synced. Each notebook sees
only its own names; a renamed or moved notebook keeps them. There is
no system permission: the first call asks the app's prompt for this
notebook, and Settings lists and deletes each notebook's secrets.

Strings a notebook keeps in the system keychain, on this device only and per notebook. Every method needs the secrets permission, which is the app's prompt alone: there is no system one. The permission methods work where the rest of the namespace does.

## `SoundPlayer`

A loaded sound a cell controls, from `device.sound.player`: a
`NativeHandle`. Close it when done, or hold it with `await using`. The
app closes a kernel's players when that kernel restarts or shuts down; a
kernel has at most 32 open. Each method answers the player's state after
the change.

Its methods work wherever [`device.sound.player`](#device-sound-player-data-options) does.

### `player.play(options?)`

```ts
play(options?: CallOptions): Promise<SoundState>;
```

Plays from the current time.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. |

**Returns** `Promise<SoundState>`: The player's state after the change.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` when the sound can't start, or the player is closed.

```ts
const state = await player.play();
console.log(state.playing, state.duration);
```

### `player.pause(options?)`

```ts
pause(options?: CallOptions): Promise<SoundState>;
```

Pauses at the current time.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. |

**Returns** `Promise<SoundState>`: The player's state after the change.

```ts
const { time } = await player.pause();
console.log(`paused at ${time.toFixed(1)} s`);
```

### `player.stop(options?)`

```ts
stop(options?: CallOptions): Promise<SoundState>;
```

Pauses and goes back to the start.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. |

**Returns** `Promise<SoundState>`: The player's state after the change.

```ts
await player.stop();
```

### `player.seek(seconds, options?)`

```ts
seek(seconds: number, options?: CallOptions): Promise<SoundState>;
```

Moves to a time, playing or not.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `seconds` | `number` | yes | The time to move to, in seconds from the start: 0 or more. |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. |

**Returns** `Promise<SoundState>`: The player's state after the change.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` when `seconds` is negative or not a number.

```ts
await player.seek(player.duration / 2);
await player.play();
```

### `player.setVolume(volume, options?)`

```ts
setVolume(volume: number, options?: CallOptions): Promise<SoundState>;
```

Sets the volume.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `volume` | `number` | yes | From 0 to 1. |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. |

**Returns** `Promise<SoundState>`: The player's state after the change.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` when `volume` is outside 0 to 1.

```ts
await player.setVolume(0.25);
```

### `player.state(options?)`

```ts
state(options?: CallOptions): Promise<SoundState>;
```

Reads the player's state, changing nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. |

**Returns** `Promise<SoundState>`: Whether it is playing, its time and its length.

```ts
const { playing, time } = await player.state();
```

### `player.close()`

```ts
close(): Promise<void>;
```

Stops the player and frees it; later calls fail `failed`. Closing
twice is fine. Leaving an `await using` block closes it too.

```ts
await player.close();
```

### Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `duration` | `number` | The sound's length in seconds. |

## `Peripheral`

A connected Bluetooth LE peripheral, from `device.bluetooth.connect`: a
`NativeHandle`. Close it to disconnect, or hold it with `await using`.
The app closes a kernel's peripherals when that kernel restarts or
shuts down; a kernel has at most 8 connected. When the peripheral goes
away, waiting calls and the next call reject `disconnected`, `notify`
streams end with it, and the handle closes (`closed` reads true once a
call has seen it). Services and characteristics are UUIDs:
"180D", or the full form.

Its methods work wherever [`device.bluetooth.connect`](#device-bluetooth-connect-id-options) does.

### `peripheral.services(options?)`

```ts
services(options?: CallOptions): Promise<BluetoothService[]>;
```

Its services and their characteristics, discovered on the first call.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<BluetoothService[]>`: Each service with its characteristics and what they allow.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `disconnected` when it went away; `failed` when it is closed or discovery fails.

```ts
for (const service of await peripheral.services()) console.log(service.uuid, service.characteristics.map((c) => c.uuid));
```

### `peripheral.read(service, characteristic, options?)`

```ts
read(service: string, characteristic: string, options?: CallOptions): Promise<Uint8Array>;
```

Reads a characteristic's value.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `service` | `string` | yes | The service's UUID. |
| `characteristic` | `string` | yes | The characteristic's UUID. |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<Uint8Array>`: The value's bytes.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `disconnected` when it went away; `failed` when it is closed, there is no such characteristic, or it can't be read.

```ts
const [level] = await peripheral.read("180F", "2A19");
console.log(`battery ${level}%`);
```

### `peripheral.write(service, characteristic, data, options?)`

```ts
write(service: string, characteristic: string, data: Bytes, options?: WriteOptions): Promise<void>;
```

Writes a characteristic's value.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `service` | `string` | yes | The service's UUID. |
| `characteristic` | `string` | yes | The characteristic's UUID. |
| `data` | `Bytes` | yes | The bytes, at most what the link takes at once (512 with a response). |
| `options` | `WriteOptions` | no | `withResponse` (true by default), and the call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`; the write may already be sent. |

**Returns** once the peripheral confirms it, or at once without a response.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `disconnected` when it went away; `failed` when it is closed, there is no such characteristic, it can't be written that way, or `data` is too long.

```ts
await peripheral.write("6E400001-B5A3-F393-E0A9-E50E24DCCA9E", "6E400002-B5A3-F393-E0A9-E50E24DCCA9E", new TextEncoder().encode("hi"));
```

### `peripheral.notify(service, characteristic, options?)`

```ts
notify(service: string, characteristic: string, options?: CallOptions): DeviceStream<Uint8Array>;
```

A characteristic's values as it notifies or indicates them, for
`for await`, until the loop ends, the cell is interrupted, or the
peripheral closes. Keeps the newest 256 when the cell reads slower
than they come.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `service` | `string` | yes | The service's UUID. |
| `characteristic` | `string` | yes | The characteristic's UUID. |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`, which ends the stream. |

**Returns** `DeviceStream<Uint8Array>`: A stream of values; leaving the loop unsubscribes.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `disconnected` when it went away; `failed` when it is closed, or there is no such characteristic or it doesn't notify.

```ts
for await (const value of peripheral.notify("180D", "2A37")) {
  console.log(`heart rate ${value[1]}`);
}
```

### `peripheral.rssi(options?)`

```ts
rssi(options?: CallOptions): Promise<number>;
```

Reads the signal strength now.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<number>`: dBm, such as -60.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `disconnected` when it went away; `failed` when it is closed.

```ts
console.log(await peripheral.rssi());
```

### Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | Its id on this device. |
| `name` | `string \| null` | Its name when it connected, or `null`. |

## `Folder`

A folder the person picked for this notebook, from
`device.folders.pick()` or `list()`. It stays this notebook's until
the person revokes it in Settings, across kernel and app restarts, so
there is nothing to close.

Each `path` is relative to the folder, with `/` between parts. An
absolute path, a `..`, or a symlink that leads outside the folder
rejects `denied`.

Its methods work wherever [`device.folders.pick`](#device-folders-pick-options) does. Paths are relative to the folder; one that leads outside it rejects `denied`.

### `folder.entries(path?, options?)`

```ts
entries(path?: string, options?: CallOptions): Promise<FolderEntry[]>;
```

Lists a directory in the folder, sorted by name.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | no | A directory in the folder; the folder itself when left out. |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<FolderEntry[]>`: Its files and directories, hidden ones included.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `denied` when the path leaves the folder or the grant was revoked; `unavailable` when the folder can't be reached now (a disconnected drive, say); `failed` when there is no directory there.

```ts
const [folder] = await device.folders.list();
for (const entry of await folder.entries()) console.log(entry.kind, entry.name, entry.size);
```

### `folder.read(path, options?)`

```ts
read(path: string, options?: CallOptions): Promise<Uint8Array>;
```

Reads a file in the folder.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | yes | The file, relative to the folder. |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<Uint8Array>`: Its bytes.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `denied` when the path leaves the folder or the grant was revoked; `unavailable` when the folder can't be reached now (a disconnected drive, say); `failed` when there is no file there or it is over 16 MiB.

```ts
const [folder] = await device.folders.list();
const csv = new TextDecoder().decode(await folder.read("data/temps.csv"));
```

### `folder.write(path, data, options?)`

```ts
write(path: string, data: Bytes | string, options?: CallOptions): Promise<void>;
```

Writes a file in the folder, replacing what is there and making the
directories on the way.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | yes | The file, relative to the folder. |
| `data` | `Bytes \| string` | yes | The bytes, at most 16 MiB, or a string written as UTF-8. |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`; the write may already be done. |

**Returns** once the file is written.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `denied` when the folder was picked for reading only, the path leaves the folder, or the grant was revoked; `unavailable` when the folder can't be reached now (a disconnected drive, say); `failed` when the path is a directory or `data` is over 16 MiB.

```ts
const folder = await device.folders.pick({ write: true });
if (folder) await folder.write("notes/today.txt", "Written from a notebook");
```

### `folder.remove(path, options?)`

```ts
remove(path: string, options?: CallOptions): Promise<void>;
```

Removes a file, a symlink (not what it points to), or an empty directory, in the folder.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | yes | What to remove, relative to the folder. |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`; it may already be removed. |

**Returns** once it is gone.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `denied` when the folder was picked for reading only, the path leaves the folder or is the folder itself, or the grant was revoked; `unavailable` when the folder can't be reached now (a disconnected drive, say); `failed` when nothing is there or a directory isn't empty.

```ts
const folder = await device.folders.pick({ write: true });
if (folder) await folder.remove("notes/old.txt");
```

### Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | Names the grant; `list()` gives the same id after a restart. |
| `name` | `string` | The folder's name, as the picker showed it. |
| `writable` | `boolean` | Whether it was picked with `write: true`. |

## Errors

A call that fails rejects with a `DeviceError`, an `Error` whose `code` says why. A person dismissing a picker or dialog is not an error.

| `code` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `unavailable` | No native host, or this platform doesn't have the feature. |
| `denied` | The person or the system refused permission. |
| `cancelled` | Interrupted or aborted before the host answered. |
| `timeout` | The call's `signal` came from `AbortSignal.timeout()` and timed out. |
| `failed` | Anything else, such as an argument the method refuses; the message says what. |
| `disconnected` | The peer went away mid-call, such as a Bluetooth device or a remote link. |

## Types

### `CallOptions`

Every method takes these. Aborting `signal`, or interrupting the kernel,
cancels the call: it rejects with a `DeviceError` whose code is
`cancelled` (`timeout` for `AbortSignal.timeout()`), and the host drops
any dialog or prompt it showed for it.

Where each method works is in `SUPPORT` (src/support.ts); the docs'
table and the reference's Availability lines are generated from it.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `signal` | `AbortSignal` | no | Cancels the call when aborted. In a cdp-kernel cell, `jupyter.signal` aborts when the cell is interrupted. |

### `DeviceInfo`

What the host answers to `hello`, once, before the first cell, and the current state when it answers `info`.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `platform` | `string` | yes | `"macos"`, `"ipados"`, `"ios"` or `"browser"`. |
| `appVersion` | `string` | yes | The app's version, such as `"0.5.0"`. |
| `model` | `string` | no | The hardware model identifier, such as `"Mac14,2"` or `"iPad13,4"`. |
| `osVersion` | `string` | no | The operating system's version, such as `"26.1.0"`. |
| `capabilities` | `string[]` | yes | The methods this host answers, such as `"clipboard.readText"`. |
| `isPad` | `boolean` | no | True on an iPad. This and the properties after it are read when `info()` is called, on hosts that answer it. |
| `screen` | `{ width: number; height: number; scale: number }` | no | The main screen in points, and its points-to-pixels scale. |
| `battery` | `{ level: number \| null; charging: boolean }` | no | Absent on a device without a battery. `level` is 0 to 1, or null when unknown. |
| `darkMode` | `boolean` | no | Whether the system appearance is dark. |
| `locale` | `string` | no | The person's locale as a BCP 47 tag, such as `"en-US"`. |

### `NativeHandle`

Something on the device a call opened that outlives the call, such as a
sound player. Close it when done, or hold it with `await using`. The app
closes a kernel's handles when that kernel restarts or shuts down. A
call on a closed handle rejects `failed`.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `closed` | `boolean` | yes | Whether it is closed: by `close()`, or by leaving its `await using` block. |
| `close` | `Promise<void>` | yes | Closes it and frees what it holds. Closing twice is fine. |

What each host event's handler gets, by event (`device.on`).

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `appearance` | `"light" \| "dark"` | yes | The system appearance changed. |
| `foreground` | `null` | yes | The app came to the front. |
| `background` | `null` | yes | The app left the front: another app is in front, or the device locked. |
| `battery` | `{ level: number \| null; charging: boolean }` | yes | The battery's level (0 to 1, or `null` when unknown) or charging changed. Never on a Mac without a battery. |
| `locale` | `string` | yes | The system language or region changed: the new locale, a BCP 47 tag such as `"fr-FR"`. |

### `AuthorizationStatus`

A capability's authorization. Partial grants count as granted:
`limited` (some contacts or photos), `writeOnly` (add reminders or
photos, not read them) and `reducedAccuracy` (approximate location).

```ts
export type AuthorizationStatus = "notDetermined" | "denied" | "restricted" | "authorized" | "limited" | "writeOnly" | "reducedAccuracy";
```
